findings.text: §7 folds `check-review`, `check-manifest`, `repair-status`, `repair-review`, `budget-lift`, `budget-lifts`, `budget-reset`, `preflight`, `resume-ready`, `redispatch` and `unwatch` out of the command tree (§1 rows :67-72) and adds `crew repair`/`crew budget`/`crew check`, but `tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py:135` asserts `set(_leaf_commands(cli_module.crew)) == set(STATE_PHRASES)` against a hardcoded one-row-per-current-leaf dict (:16-67, with `check-review`, `check-manifest`, `repair-status`, `repair-review`, `budget-lift`, `budget-lifts`, `budget-reset`, `preflight`, `resume-ready`, `redispatch`, `unwatch` present and no `repair`/`budget`/`check`), so the fold reddens it; that file is in no section's write paths (§6 and §7 both change the leaf set and neither lists it), and the done-when instead predicts the opposite, that "the two tests that fail at base because check-review and repair-review lack a help-state row and a skill citation pass once those verbs fold" while excluding it from the pass list. Measured at base `b5ebad09`: `tests/test_crew_help_names_its_state.py` passes (5 passed) and `tests/test_skill_contracts.py tests/test_cited_commands_exist.py` pass (74 passed) — the claimed base failure does not exist, and the tests that will break are the ones the node is not fenced to edit.
